title: Women Film Composers Remain Underrepresented as Bold New Scores Break Through
excerpt:
Only eight of 2026’s top 100 box-office films feature original scores by women.
New projects spotlight inventive music and the personal stories behind it.
body_md:
Women remain significantly underrepresented among the composers behind Hollywood’s biggest releases, even as several of the year’s most distinctive scores and documentary projects demonstrate the breadth of their work. According to figures cited for 2026, just eight of the top 100 grossing films feature original scores composed by women. That follows two years in which the share ranged from seven to nine percent, down from 14 percent in 2023.

One of the most personal projects in this conversation is *Cosmic Symphony*, a documentary short directed by composer Laura Karpman. The film follows four musicians who lost treasured instruments in the January 2025 Los Angeles fires. Among them are songwriter Diane Warren, jazz bassist John Clayton, composer Starr Parodi and educator Susie Chung. Their stories explore how an instrument can become a repository of memories, collaborations and artistic identity, making its destruction far more than a financial loss.

Karpman also composed the documentary’s music, combining orchestral and choral textures. Animation helps bring the lost instruments and their histories back into focus. The project marks a move into directing for an artist already known for her work in film and television scoring.

Elsewhere, Scottish composer Anna Meredith took an unusually intimate approach to the fantasy romance *Wicker*. Rather than building a conventional large-scale orchestral soundtrack, she worked with a small ensemble featuring viola, cello and recorders of different sizes. The contrast between wind and string textures helps distinguish the central relationship from the surrounding community, allowing musical timbre to carry part of the storytelling.

For *Tenzing*, composer Rebekka Karijord sought collaboration with Nepalese musicians and performers to connect the score more closely to the film’s Himalayan setting and subject. Traditional vocal performances and recorded regional sounds sit alongside orchestral forces, creating a musical language that reflects both the mountain’s physical danger and its spiritual significance.

Taken together, these projects reveal a striking contrast: women composers are producing adventurous, deeply researched and emotionally resonant work, yet their representation in mainstream box-office filmmaking remains stubbornly low. Recognition during awards season may raise their visibility, but lasting change would require more consistent opportunities across major productions.
seo_title: Women Film Composers in 2026: New Scores, Persistent Gap
seo_description: Women scored just eight of 2026's top 100 grossing films, while Cosmic Symphony, Wicker and Tenzing showcase inventive new work.
